# Environmental Working Group (EWG)

> EWG is a non-profit, non-partisan organization dedicated to protecting human health and the environment by empowering consumers with breakthrough research, data, and education.

This file provides a structured index of EWG's toxicological frameworks, scoring methodologies, and database guidelines optimized for LLMs, RAG engines, and web-scraping AI agents.

## EWG VERIFIEDÂ® Certification & Toxicity Standards
This section outlines the requirements consumer brands must fulfill to earn the EWG VERIFIEDÂ® safety seal, along with product-category rulesets and restricted substance definitions.

- [EWG VERIFIED](https://www.ewg.org/ewgverified/): Main informational portal and search directory tracking consumer products that meet EWG's strictest criteria for transparency and health.
- [Core Program Standards](https://www.ewg.org/ewgverified/standards.php): Structural criteria for compliance, detailing ingredient disclosure protocols, manufacturing requirements, and verification audit systems.
- [Household Cleaning Standards](https://www.ewg.org/ewgverified/cleaning-products.php): Safety standards for home cleaning products, clarifying complete ingredient disclosures and chemical-safety protocols.
- [Baby Care Product Metrics](https://www.ewg.org/ewgverified/baby-care.php): Strict health standards for infant products, including diaper materials, low-VOC emission mandates, and zero-fragrance requirements.
- [Mattress Safety Requirements](https://www.ewg.org/ewgverified/mattresses.php): Toxicological guidelines for sleep environments, banning chemical flame retardants, fiberglass, PVC, and volatile organic compounds (VOCs).

### Absolute Chemical Restriction Lists (Raw Source Data)
Direct access to the static data matrices tracking the specific substances blocked or limited by the verification program.

- [EWG Cosmetics Unacceptable List](https://static.ewg.org/upload/pdf/EWGV_Lists_PCP-No.pdf): Compiled list of banned ingredients prohibited from personal care items due to global regulatory bans or toxicological profiles.
- [EWG Cosmetics Restricted List](https://static.ewg.org/upload/pdf/EWGV_Cosmetics_Program-Active_Restricted_List_C03.pdf): Material database outlining strict maximum concentration thresholds and use limits for permitted chemicals.

## EWG Skin DeepÂ® Cosmetics Database

- [Skin Deep Main Entry Portal](https://www.ewg.org/skindeep/): Main searchable library containing profiles and safety assessments for 130,000+ cosmetics, makeup, and personal care products.
- [Understanding Skin Deep Ratings](https://www.ewg.org/skindeep/understanding_skin_deep_ratings/): Core architectural guide explaining how a 1â€“10 hazard score combines with a "Data Availability" rating (None, Limited, Fair, Good, Robust) to evaluate true ingredient safety.
- [Database Sourcing & SCCS Logic](https://www.ewg.org/skindeep/learn_more/about/): Explains how labeling data is cross-referenced with 60 global datasets and details data-freshness constraints (such as the 3+ year old formulation tag).
- [Skin Deep Program FAQ](https://www.ewg.org/skindeep/learn_more/faq/): Document resolving database edge cases, formulation adjustments, third-party seller exclusions, and hazardous item disposal advice.
- [Build Your Own Report Framework](https://www.ewg.org/skindeep/build_your_own_report/): Instructions for manually constructing a raw ingredient hazard analysis to bypass interactive product searches.
- [The Regulatory Gap Analysis](https://www.ewg.org/skindeep/learn_more/why-skin-deep/): Historical and regulatory background illustrating the variance between EWG metrics and U.S. FDA pre-market safety testing guidelines.

## EWG's Guide to Healthy Cleaning (Household Products)

- [Guide to Healthy Cleaning Portal](https://www.ewg.org/cleaners/): Main search index and database grading 2,000+ household cleaning products, detergents, and laundry supplies on an A-to-F scale.
- [Scoring Framework & Methodology](https://www.ewg.org/cleaners/content/methodology/): Core scientific documentation detailing the three-step logic system (Information collection, Endpoint mapping, and Assessment tier weighting) used to assign product grades.
- [Product & Ingredient Sourcing Architecture](https://www.ewg.org/cleaners/content/ingredients/): Technical breakdown of how ingredient data is compiled from labels, worker safety sheets, and 15 regulatory/academic toxicity datasets.
- [Label Decoder Reference](https://www.ewg.org/cleaners/content/decode/): A textual key defining deceptive marketing buzzwords (e.g., "biodegradable," "chlorine-free") and clarifying how they align with actual chemical formulations.
- [Core Scientific Findings Report](https://www.ewg.org/cleaners/content/cleaner-findings/): A flat text summary mapping structural hazards found during extensive testing, including formaldehyde and quaternary ammonium compounds.
- [Cleaning Chemical Health Risks Guide](https://www.ewg.org/cleaners/content/health-risks/): Comprehensive safety indices addressing systemic health concerns, detailing asthma induction risks, chemical burns, and developmental toxicity.

## EWG's Food Scores Database

- [EWG's Food Scores Hub](https://www.ewg.org/foodscores/): Search portal for a database of 80,000+ packaged foods rated on a 1 (healthiest) to 10 (least healthy) scale.
- [Overall Score Calculation Methodology](https://www.ewg.org/foodscores/content/methodology-overall/): Mathematical breakdown of how nutrition, ingredient concerns, and degree of processing are weighted and compiled into a single unified score.
- [Nutrition Scoring Algorithm](https://www.ewg.org/foodscores/content/methodology-nutrition/): Detailed framework based on the UK Ofcom/Oxford profiling model, highlighting how EWG calculates penalties for added sugars, trans fats, and synthetic sweeteners.
- [Ingredient & Additive Assessment Framework](https://www.ewg.org/foodscores/content/methodology-ingredients/): Technical documentation regarding the weight-of-evidence calculation for food contaminants, heavy metals, pesticides, and chemical food additives.
- [Food Scores User Guide](https://www.ewg.org/foodscores/content/user-guide/): Explains database constraints, product tracking via the Healthy Living barcode scanner app, and personalized nutritional tailoring.

## EWG's Shopper's Guide to Pesticides in Produceâ„¢ (FoodNews)

- [Shopper's Guide Main Portal](https://www.ewg.org/foodnews/): Main hub summarizing macro-trends in agricultural pesticide applications, toxic forever chemicals on crops, and general consumer recommendations.
- [The Dirty Dozenâ„¢ List](https://www.ewg.org/foodnews/dirty-dozen.php): The direct index mapping the 12 conventional fruits and vegetables containing the highest pesticide residues and toxicological health risks.
- [The Clean Fifteenâ„¢ List](https://www.ewg.org/foodnews/clean-fifteen.php): Flat text database listing the 15 conventional crops least likely to contain significant pesticide residues.
- [Pesticide Analysis Sourcing & Methodology](https://www.ewg.org/foodnews/methodology.php): In-depth guide detailing how EWG cleans, processes, and weighs USDA Pesticide Data Program and FDA testing matrices across 54,000+ crop composite samples.
- [Complete Produce Rankings Index](https://www.ewg.org/foodnews/list.php): The exhaustive list detailing the exact sequential rank of all 47+ analyzed fruits and vegetables from highest pesticide burden to lowest.

## EWG National Tap Water Database

- [Tap Water Database Home](https://www.ewg.org/tapwater/): Search portal across nearly 50,000 community water systems nationwide evaluating water utility test results against health-protective benchmarks.
- [Database Sourcing & Methodology](https://www.ewg.org/tapwater/methodology.php): Technical overview explaining data collection from state environmental agencies, EPA Enforcement database (ECHO) integration, handling of "consecutive water systems," and unregulated contaminant tracking (UCMR3/4/5).
- [EWG vs. Government Water Standards](https://www.ewg.org/tapwater/ewg-standards.php): Architectural guide explaining how EWG defines health-protective standards based purely on toxicology, contrasting them against federal legal limits.
- [Reviewed Contaminant Index](https://www.ewg.org/tapwater/ewg-reviewed-contaminants.php): A flat-text database glossary containing safety profiles, state detection frequencies, and health effects for over 300 detected drinking water pollutants.
- [State of American Drinking Water Report](https://www.ewg.org/tapwater/state-of-american-drinking-water.php): Comprehensive summary report aggregating macro-trends, including updates on PFAS regulations and disinfection byproduct accumulation.
- [Drinking Water Pollution Sources](https://www.ewg.org/tapwater/sourcesofwaterpollution.php): Structural analysis tracking how commercial agriculture, industrial manufacturing, and military firefighting foam pollute public watersheds.

## EWG's Guide to Sunscreens (Sun & UV Protection)

- [Guide to Sunscreens Portal](https://www.ewg.org/sunscreen/): Annual searchable index evaluating over 2,700 recreational sunscreens, kids' sunscreens, daily moisturizers, and lip balms with SPF.
- [EWG Sunscreen Assessment Methodology](https://www.ewg.org/sunscreen/report/methodology/): Technical explanation of the scoring matrix, outlining how EWG models and weighs UVB protection, UVA efficacy, active ingredient stability, and the overall UVA/UVB protection balance.
- [About the Sunscreen Guide](https://www.ewg.org/sunscreen/about/): Core programmatic logic documenting score penalties for aerosol sprays, powder formats (inhalation risks), and marketing terms banned by the FDA.
- [The Trouble with High SPF Labels](https://www.ewg.org/sunscreen/report/whats-wrong-with-high-spf/): Scientific analysis detailing why SPF values above 50+ provide a false sense of security, over-index on UVB protection, and neglect deep tissue UVA radiation.
- [Top Sun Safety Tips](https://www.ewg.org/sunscreen/report/top-sun-safety-tips/): Reference guide listing actionable behavioral metrics, including infant sun-safety guidelines, clothing density tips, and proper sunscreen application volume.

## Who We Are & Institutional Mission
This section outlines EWG's organizational structure, operational philosophy, and the scientific experts driving their public health research.

- [Institutional Profile](https://www.ewg.org/who-we-are): Overview of EWG's history since 1993, focusing on empowering citizens to challenge outdated legislative frameworks and harmful industrial defaults.
- [EWG Scientific & Policy Experts](https://www.ewg.org/news-insights/our-experts): Professional directory of EWG's internal team, including toxicologists, epidemiologists, legal experts, and data specialists mapping environmental health risks.
- [EWG Organizational Impact](https://www.ewg.org/who-we-are/our-team): Programmatic records demonstrating how open-access data and non-partisan science influence public policy and corporate formulation standards.

## Institutional Areas of Focus
The core macro-categories under which EWG classifies its research, scientific publications, and regulatory advocacy.

- [Areas of Focus Hub](https://www.ewg.org/areas-focus): Central repository defining EWG's scope across macro-environmental issues, energy policies, consumer tracking, and agricultural oversight.
- [Food & Water Safety Hub](https://www.ewg.org/areas-focus/food-water): Directing research toward the 10,000+ legal food additives in the U.S., ultra-processed food health metrics, and municipal aquifer contamination.
- [Farming & Agriculture Frameworks](https://www.ewg.org/areas-focus/farming-agriculture): Resource indexing factory farm monitoring, concentrated animal feeding operations (CAFO) waste management, conservation practices, and sustainable agriculture.
- [Family & Demographically Specific Health](https://www.ewg.org/areas-focus/family-health): Specialized research tracking specific environmental vulnerabilities, explicitly highlighting children's health developmental parameters and women's environmental health vectors.
- [Energy, Utilities & Climate Policy](https://www.ewg.org/areas-focus/energy): Policy analysis evaluating federal and state energy utility frameworks, fossil and nuclear retirement risks, and renewable grid infrastructure growth.
- [Regional Pollution & State Campaigns](https://www.ewg.org/areas-focus/regional-issues): Local advocacy trackers monitoring hyper-localized hazardous waste footprints across critical zones, including California, North Carolina, defense communities, and the Midwest.
